LESSON: MODELLING AND ORNAMENT MAKING.

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Performing and Display
Topic 2.6: Modelling and Ornament Making.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Modelling and Ornament Making., part of Performing and Display in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How are ornaments made?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify modelled beads for familiarity,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Modelling and Ornament Making. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. model beads using pellet technique,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Modelling and Ornament Making. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. decorate the beads

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Modelling and Ornament Making. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. make a beaded ornament,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Modelling and Ornament Making. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appraise own and others modelled items for appreciation. ● Learners are guided to explore virtual and actual samples of modelled beads while learners with blindness are given description of virtual aspects that require use of sight. ● Learners with low vision are guided to model beads using pellet technique. Learners with blindness are given one on one demonstration to model beads using pellet technique. ● In groups, learners are guided to decorate the beads. ● In groups, learners are guided to model. How are ornaments made? 38 ● Learners with low vision paint the beads in two different colours while learners with blindness manipulate the modelled beads and describe their texture. ● Learners are guided to display items made for peers’ feedback.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Modelling and Ornament Making. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Modelling and Ornament Making. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: A learner works together to prepare clay or peppier Mache for modelling items.

• Creativity and imagination: A learner develops creativity to make a single stranded necklace and a matching bracelet.

Values:
● Respect: A learner gives positive feedback as they display items made.

● Unity: A learner in groups, prepare clay or peppier Mache for modelling items.

● Patriotism: A learner takes pride in making ornaments using recyclable materials from the local community.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Safety and security: A learner observes their safety as they fire the clay beads in an improvised kiln.

• Social cohesion: A learner portrays team spirit as they explore pinch and pellet technique to make simple forms in pairs.

39

Link to other subjects:

• Environmental Activities: Learner applies knowledge and skills gained in Environmental Activities to create melodic

patterns from differently pitched objects such as voiced or tuned percussion.
